flawed_step: Lines 10 and 18 establish only that g is a monomorphism from Z into D; they do not establish the stated claim that it maps onto D. That claim is false in general.
counterexample: Take D = Q with its usual ordering. It is an ordered integral domain, and g(n)=n·1_Q=n. But g is not onto Q: for example, 1/2 is not g(n) for any integer n.
assessment_summary: The claimed surjectivity onto every ordered integral domain fails for D=Q, so the theorem as stated and its proof are invalid.
